title: Level 2 (Intermediate) - D-27
notes:
West leads the ♠4 against 3NT. East wins the first trick with the ♠K and returns the ♠5. The good news for South is that the spot cards played by the defenders strongly suggest that spades are 4-4. The bad news is that South is faced with a guess in spades at trick 2.

On the above layout, South must play the ♠10 in order to have a chance to make 3NT. West will win the ♠A, but South's ♠Q will stop the suit. If, however, East was dealt the ♠A and the ♠J is with West, then South must play the ♠Q instead of the ♠10 to stop the spades.

The percentage play is for South to finesse the ♠10 because East is twice as likely to hold honor-Jack of spades than both top honors (♠KJ or ♠AJ (2 cases) to ♠AK (1 case)). On the actual layout the percentage play is rewarded when West wins the ♠A and clears the suit.

On the assumption that the defenders' spades were dealt 4-4, South can afford to lose a club trick (as he will lose only 4 tricks in total - 1 club and 3 spades). South should duck the first round of clubs completely as a safety play against West holding all 4 outstanding clubs.

East's discard on the first round of clubs reveals the 4-0 club break so that South's first-round club duck was a necessary precaution. The defense will cash a spade trick and play a heart to South. South easily wins the rest of the tricks with the help of the marked finesse in clubs. If both defenders had followed to the first round of clubs, the suit would now run as cashing the ♣A and ♣K would drop all the remaining clubs.
